industry.b2b: IndiaMART is a classifieds-style marketplace, not a transaction platform: it does not take a commission on the deal, hold inventory or handle payment (a buyer-payment protection programme for TrustSEAL sellers started in 2026). It sells visibility and buy leads to suppliers on annual and multi-year subscriptions. Survey data: ~40-45% of buyers who respond say they procured through IndiaMART; 90-day buyer repeat rate 58-59% (up from 50-51%) (Q1FY27 call).
industry.market: ~1.6 crore GST-registered businesses (about half with turnover below Rs40 lakh, 85% proprietorships); ~50 lakh GST-identified sellers registered on IndiaMART, 2.2 lakh paying; management puts free-tier penetration of the serviceable market at ~50% (Q4FY26 call).
industry.competition: Horizontal B2B listings: Justdial (local search, Reliance-owned), TradeIndia, Google search and Maps; vertical and transactional B2B platforms (Udaan, Moglix, OfBusiness, Amazon Business, Industry Buying, in which IndiaMART holds 21%); ONDC. The new threat is AI assistants answering procurement queries without sending traffic to listing sites: management calls it 'a two-way sword' (Q1FY27 call).
industry.traffic: IndiaMART stopped reporting traffic about a year before Q1FY27 because bot, agent and LLM traffic made it hard to classify; it spends Rs7-8 cr a quarter on buyer advertising in its top-10% categories and is moving to 100% OTP buyer verification behind log-in (Q1FY27 call).
industry.accountingSoftware: Tally holds 60-70% of the MSME accounting-software market (management, Q1FY27 call); Busy, Vyapar (28.6% associate), Realbooks and Livekeeping (a cloud/mobile layer on Tally) are IndiaMART's bets in the category.

peers.approach: Natural set: the internet platforms in our library (Eternal, Swiggy, Info Edge, Nykaa, Paytm, PB Fintech; IRCTC, ETERNAL, NAUKRI and PWL reports). Excluding IndiaMART itself, only Info Edge has a usable five-year P/E history, so per the thin-peer-set rule we widen to the next-closest group the market and brokers use for IndiaMART: listed online classifieds and listings businesses (Screener's peer group 'Internet & Catalogue Retail': Info Edge, Just Dial, Matrimony.com; plus CarTrade, the other listed classifieds platform in the Nifty India Internet index).

excluded.CARTRADE: Online auto classifieds, but loss-making in FY22 (EPS -Rs28): P/E negative for about a fifth of the five-year window.
excluded.ETERNAL: Losses or near-zero profit for most of FY22-FY24; P/E above 1,000x inside the window.
excluded.NYKAA: P/E above 1,000x inside the window (profit near zero).
excluded.POLICYBZR: Loss-making until FY24; P/E above 1,000x inside the window.
excluded.NAZARA: Gaming platform in the Nifty India Internet index; EPS near zero (P/E 100-280x in 2021-25) and Screener's P/E history breaks in 2026 on share-count adjustments: distorted.
excluded.AFFLE: Ad-tech; in the Nifty India Digital index, not the Internet index, and not a listings business: not in the set.

peers.note: Info Edge (Naukri: job classifieds) is used despite its fair-value-distorted P/E, as in the IRCTC and Physicswallah reports. Just Dial's FY22 profit fell to Rs8.5 a share after the Reliance takeover (P/E up to ~270x in 2022); it is kept because it stayed profitable every year and its P/E never crossed the ~300x line used for the internet set, but a set without it is shown as a sensitivity. The internet-only and classifieds-only sub-sets and no move are sensitivity rows (PLAYBOOK §7c).

street.history: MOSL targets: Rs3,500 (Oct-2024), Rs3,050 (Jul-2025), Rs2,900 (Oct-2025), Rs2,750 (Jan-2026), Rs2,500 (May-2026), Rs2,250 (Jul-2026); Axis: Rs3,620 (Oct-2024) to Rs2,060 (Jul-2026) (Trendlyne research list).
street.method: The street values IndiaMART on P/E on FY28E EPS (Choice 20x FY28E); MOSL uses a DCF whose target equals ~21x its FY28E EPS. No broker visible to us uses a sum-of-the-parts for the strategic stakes.

critiques: Bull: a debt-free, cash-rich platform at ~16x Sep-28E EPS that still grows revenue ~10% and EPS ~13% a year on price increases, with deferred revenue up 16%
Bear: the paying-supplier base has not grown for two years (217K Mar-25, 218K Jun-26); growth rests on raising prices on the same customers, which the Silver price rise showed has limits

Bear: buyer enquiries and active buyers are falling (UBE ~26 Mn, active buyers -5% YoY per an analyst on the call) while search moves to AI assistants that may answer procurement questions without sending the lead
Bear: margins are high because acquisition spending is low; reigniting supplier growth would cost margin (management: sustained leverage needs subscriber growth)
Bear: ~Rs750 cr of minority start-up stakes, equity-accounted losses of ~Rs55 cr a year and fair-value gains that flatter reported EPS
Bull: Busy plus IndiaMART Finance (transaction credit with partner lenders) and buyer monetisation are optionality not in estimates

governance.board: Founder-led: Dinesh Agarwal (MD & CEO) and Brijesh Agrawal (WTD) with WTD Manoj Bhargava; independent directors include Pallavi Dinodia Gupta, Manish Vij and Aakash Chaudhry among others (AR FY24/FY26).
governance.pay: CEO Rs8.33 cr (165x median), WTD Rs6.17 cr (122x median) in FY26; ESOP cost Rs36.6 cr (2.3% of revenue).
governance.relatedParty: Strategic stakes in 13 start-ups (associates and FVTPL investees) and follow-on rounds decided by management; IndiaMART holds up to ~34.5% of some investees and fair-values others, which moves reported profit.
governance.capitalReturn: ~Rs1,650 cr returned to shareholders since FY21 (dividends and an FY24 buyback); FY26 payout 76% including a special dividend.

conflicts: Q1FY27 consolidated EBITDA: Rs146.4 cr (MOSL, company) vs Screener operating profit Rs132 cr: Screener deducts the Rs14.6 cr share of associates' losses inside expenses. Our model follows Screener (EBITDA after associates) and the text quotes the company basis where stated.
Choice's note says paying suppliers 'declined by ~18,500' in Q1FY27; the company reported a net decline of ~1,850. We use the company figure.
Paying suppliers YoY: deck shows 218K in both Q1FY26 and Q1FY27 (0%); management's FY26 commentary cites +3.2K net adds for the year (217K to 220K).
MOSL treats Rs8.5 cr of Q3FY26 labour-code cost as exceptional; the company reports it inside employee costs (AR FY26). We follow the company.
